summary: Algoma District tower about 1 km west of Saunders Lake, cupola still in place, reached by an unmarked old trail.

visit.trail_note: About 1 km west from Saunders Lake; the trail is unmarked and gains about 61 m (200 ft). Route from Highway 17 at Thessalon via Highway 638, Highway 670 and Shaw Road.

evidence.supports: About 1 km trail west from the lake to the tower
evidence.quote: There is a 1 km trail heading west from Saunders Lake to the tower.

evidence.supports: One of the last towers built in Algoma District
evidence.quote: It is also one of the last Fire Lookout Towers to be constructed in the Algoma District.
This tower is in incredibly good shape, including the Cupola.
The hike to the tower from the main road is considered 'easy' with only a gradual grade heading upward.

evidence.supports: Former tower-man cabin on a point on the north-west shore
evidence.quote: The former tower man cabin is on the North-West shore of the lake, on a point.

evidence.supports: Route from Highway 17 at Thessalon via Highway 638 and Hwy 670
evidence.quote: From Highway 17 in Thessalon, Ontario turn onto Highway 638 and follow it for about 30km then turn left onto Hwy 670 for 9 km.

evidence.supports: Shaw Road leg of the route

evidence.quote: The trail is an old road
The trail to the tower isn’t marked

evidence.supports: Trail starts across the road from the north-west tip of the lake
evidence.quote: is located across the road from the north-west tip of the lake

evidence.supports: Gain of about 200 ft from start to finish
evidence.quote: a gain of about 200 ft from beginning to end

evidence.supports: Hiker found the cupola still in place
evidence.quote: It was great to see that this tower even still had the Cupola!

evidence.supports: List entry for Saunders Lake tower with no asterisk
Asterisk means cupola removed and tower now used as communications tower
MNR no longer maintains these towers; visitors asked not to climb
evidence.quote: The MNR no longer maintains them so please refrain from climbing.

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder, design type beyond the cupola, height or owning agency appears in any source read. The superiorhiking.com post is undated. The still-standing list is undated apart from a 2013 reference about MNR plans. No source describes ownership or whether the public may visit; the route is from hiking accounts only. Firelookout.ca lists the tower as in good shape, which the list's cupola legend is consistent with.
